name: Gotama Buddha
summary: Siddhattha Gotama of the Sakyan clan, the Buddha of this age: after going forth and six years of striving he awakened under the Bodhi tree at Uruvelā, taught the middle way and the four noble truths at Isipatana, founded the Saṅgha of monks and nuns, taught for forty-five years in the middle Ganges region and attained final nibbāna at Kusinārā at eighty. He calls himself the Tathāgata; the texts present him as the rediscoverer of an ancient path (SN 12.65) and the seventh Buddha of ninety-one aeons (DN 14).

tradition.text: born 623 BCE, awakened 588 BCE, parinibbāna 543 BCE (Theravāda Buddhist-era reckoning; Buddhist Era counted from 544/543 BCE)

scholarly.text: c. 5th c. BCE; the parinibbāna is placed c. 486 BCE on the 'corrected long chronology' or c. 400 BCE (±20) on the 'short chronology' now preferred by many scholars

realization_account.text: After six years of striving and the rejection of self-mortification, he recalled the first jhāna, took food, entered the four jhānas and in the three watches of the night attained recollection of past lives, the divine eye and the destruction of the effluents with knowledge of the four truths; 'unshakeable is my liberation, this is my last birth' (MN 26, MN 36, MN 4; SN 56.11; Vin Mv 1.1).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Scholarly datings are metadata only; the tradition's account is kept apart.

name: Sāriputta
summary: The Buddha's right-hand chief disciple, foremost in wisdom; a brahmin (Upatissa) from Nālaka, formerly a pupil of Sañjaya, converted by Assaji's verse 'ye dhammā hetuppabhavā'; expounder of MN 9, 28, 43, 141, DN 33–34 and many Nikāya discourses, and by tradition of the Paṭisambhidāmagga and Niddesa; he died shortly before the Buddha (SN 47.13).

realization_account.text: Became a stream-enterer on hearing Assaji's verse (Vin Mv 1.23); by the commentarial account attained arahantship a fortnight after ordination while fanning the Buddha during the discourse to Dīghanakha (MN 74).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Mahāmoggallāna
summary: The left-hand chief disciple, foremost in psychic power; Kolita, Sāriputta's friend, converted with him; the Buddha instructed him against drowsiness (AN 7.61); visits to heavens and hells in the Vimānavatthu and Petavatthu; by the commentarial account killed by bandits shortly before the Buddha's death.

realization_account.text: Attained arahantship seven days after ordination after the Buddha's instruction on drowsiness (AN 7.61, commentarial setting).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ānanda
summary: The Buddha's cousin and personal attendant for twenty-five years, foremost in learning, memory, attentiveness and service; interceded for women's going forth (Cv 10.1); recited the Dhamma at the First Council; many suttas are his teaching (MN 52, MN 108, SN 22.83, AN 4.170).

realization_account.text: Attained arahantship during the night before the First Council, as he was lying down, before his head reached the pillow (Cullavagga 11).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Mahākassapa
summary: Foremost in the ascetic practices (dhutaṅga); a brahmin (Pippali) who renounced with his wife Bhaddā Kāpilānī; exchanged robes with the Buddha (SN 16.11); convened and presided over the First Council at Rājagaha (Cv 11); verses at Thag 18.1.

name: Upāli
summary: The Sakyan princes' barber who went forth with them and was ordained before them; foremost in knowledge of the Vinaya; questioned by Mahākassapa on the discipline at the First Council (Cv 11.1.7).

name: Anuruddha
summary: The Buddha's Sakyan cousin, foremost in the divine eye; practised with Nandiya and Kimbila (MN 31, MN 128); his eight thoughts of a great person (AN 8.30); present at the Buddha's parinibbāna (DN 16) and, by commentarial account, entrusted with the Aṅguttara.
notes: AN 1 Etadaggavagga (the 'foremost' lists). Distinct from the later Abhidhamma author tch:anuruddha-acariya.

name: Mahākaccāna
summary: Foremost in expanding in detail what the Buddha said in brief (MN 18, MN 133, MN 138); from Avanti; tradition ascribes the Nettippakaraṇa and Peṭakopadesa to him.

name: Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta
summary: Foremost among Dhamma speakers; explains the seven purifications to Sāriputta with the relay of chariots (MN 24); taught Ānanda (SN 22.83).

name: Puṇṇa of Sunāparanta
summary: The monk who resolved to live among the fierce people of Sunāparanta with unconditional patience (MN 145; SN 35.88).

name: Mahākoṭṭhita
summary: Foremost in analytical knowledge; questioner of Sāriputta in MN 43 and SN 12.67.

name: Aññāsi Koṇḍañña
summary: The first of the five monks; the first to understand the first discourse ('whatever is subject to arising is subject to cessation', SN 56.11), hence 'Koṇḍañña who has understood'; foremost in seniority.

realization_account.text: The Dhamma-eye arose in him during the first discourse; he became an arahant with the Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta (SN 56.11; SN 22.59; Vin Mv 1.6).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vappa
summary: One of the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā) to whom the first discourse was taught at Isipatana; became an arahant with the Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta (Vin Mv 1.6).

name: Bhaddiya
summary: One of the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā) to whom the first discourse was taught at Isipatana; became an arahant with the Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta (Vin Mv 1.6).

name: Mahānāma (of the five monks)
summary: One of the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā) to whom the first discourse was taught at Isipatana; became an arahant with the Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta (Vin Mv 1.6).

name: Assaji
summary: One of the five monks; his bearing on alms round drew Sāriputta, to whom he spoke the verse 'ye dhammā hetuppabhavā' (Vin Mv 1.23).

name: Yasa
summary: A wealthy young man of Benares who went forth after hearing the Buddha's gradual talk; his parents became the first lay followers taking the three refuges (Vin Mv 1.7–8).

name: Uruvela Kassapa
summary: Leader of a thousand matted-hair fire-worshipping ascetics at Uruvelā, converted with his brothers Nadī Kassapa and Gayā Kassapa; they heard the Fire Sermon at Gayāsīsa (Vin Mv 1.15–21).

name: Rāhula
summary: The Buddha's son, given the going forth as a boy by Sāriputta (Vin Mv 1.54); instructed in MN 61, 62 and 147; foremost in desire for training.

name: Nanda
summary: The Buddha's half-brother, son of Mahāpajāpatī, who went forth reluctantly and was led by the Buddha to overcome his longing (Ud 3.2); foremost in guarding the sense doors.

name: Aṅgulimāla
summary: A murderer who wore a garland of fingers, stopped by the Buddha ('I have stopped, you stop'), who went forth and became an arahant; his act of truth for a woman in labour is used as a paritta (MN 86; Thag 16.8).

name: Bāhiya Dārucīriya
summary: A bark-clothed ascetic of Suppāraka who received the brief teaching 'in the seen only the seen' on the road and was at once liberated; foremost in quick understanding (Ud 1.10).

realization_account.text: Liberated on hearing the brief teaching; died soon after (Ud 1.10).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vakkali
summary: A monk devoted to gazing at the Buddha's body, told 'whoever sees the Dhamma sees me' (SN 22.87); foremost in faith.

name: Māluṅkyaputta
summary: The monk who demanded answers to the undeclared questions (MN 63) and who, in old age, received the 'in the seen only the seen' teaching (SN 35.95).

name: Soṇa Koḷivisa
summary: A monk whose feet bled from over-exertion, taught by the simile of the lute (AN 6.55; Vin Mv 5.1); foremost in energy.

name: Khemaka
summary: A sick elder who explained the residual conceit 'I am' in one who does not regard any aggregate as self (SN 22.89).

name: Yamaka
summary: A monk freed by Sāriputta from the view that the arahant is annihilated at death (SN 22.85).

name: Anurādha
summary: A monk questioned by wanderers about the Tathāgata after death (SN 22.86; SN 44.2).

name: Sāti Kevaṭṭaputta
summary: The fisherman's son who held that the same consciousness transmigrates, rebuked by the Buddha (MN 38).

name: Nārada (SN 12.68)
summary: An elder who had seen 'the cessation of becoming is nibbāna' but was not yet an arahant — like one who sees water in a well without a rope (SN 12.68).

name: Meghiya
summary: The Buddha's attendant who left to meditate in a mango grove and was overcome by unwholesome thoughts; taught the five things that ripen the liberation of mind (Ud 4.1; AN 9.3).

name: Girimānanda
summary: A sick monk to whom Ānanda recited the ten perceptions, after which he recovered (AN 10.60).

name: Nandaka
summary: The monk who exhorted Mahāpajāpatī's five hundred nuns (MN 146); foremost in exhorting nuns.

name: Cunda the novice
summary: Sāriputta's younger brother and attendant who brought his relics to the Buddha (SN 47.13).

name: Kumārakassapa
summary: An elder, foremost in variegated speech, who answered Pāyāsi's denial of the other world with similes (DN 23); the Vammika Sutta (MN 23) was addressed to him.

name: Purāṇa
summary: An elder who, after the First Council, said he would remember the Dhamma and discipline as he had heard them from the Buddha (Cv 11.1.11).

name: Devadatta
summary: The Buddha's cousin and monk who sought leadership of the Saṅgha, plotted against the Buddha with Ajātasattu, proposed five compulsory austerities and caused the first schism (Cv 7).

name: Subhadda the wanderer
summary: The last person ordained by the Buddha, taught that ascetics are found only where the eightfold path is found (DN 16).

name: Vaṅgīsa
summary: The poet-monk, foremost in inspired speech, whose verses fill SN 8 and Thag 21.1.

name: Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja
summary: Foremost among lion-roarers; rebuked by the Buddha for displaying psychic power to win a sandalwood bowl (Vin Cv 5.8).

name: Subhūti
summary: Anāthapiṇḍika's brother, foremost in dwelling without conflict and in being worthy of gifts; his verse opens the Theragāthā (Thag 1.1).

name: Channa
summary: The charioteer of the bodhisatta's renunciation, later an obstinate monk on whom the 'higher penalty' (brahmadaṇḍa) was imposed after the parinibbāna (DN 16; Cv 11.1.12).
notes: The Channa of SN 22.90 and MN 144 is identified with him by some commentaries; not asserted here.

name: Sudinna Kalandaputta
summary: The monk on whose account the first pārājika rule was laid down (Vin Pār 1).

name: Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī
summary: The Buddha's maternal aunt and foster-mother; first bhikkhunī, ordained on accepting the eight principles of respect (Cv 10.1; AN 8.51); foremost in seniority; her verses at Thig 6.6.

name: Khemā
summary: Former queen of King Bimbisāra, foremost nun in wisdom; taught King Pasenadi on the undeclared (SN 44.1); verses at Thig 6.3.

name: Uppalavaṇṇā
summary: Foremost nun in psychic power; verses at Thig 11.1; answers Māra in SN 5.5.

name: Paṭācārā
summary: Foremost nun in knowledge of the Vinaya; her verses tell of her liberation at a lamp's going out (Thig 5.10); by the commentarial account she had lost husband, children and parents in a single day; teacher of many nuns (Thig 5.11, 6.1).

name: Dhammadinnā
summary: Foremost nun among Dhamma teachers; her answers to Visākha in MN 44 were approved by the Buddha; verse at Thig 1.12.

name: Kisāgotamī
summary: Foremost nun in wearing coarse robes; her verses tell of the deaths of her family and her attainment of the deathless (Thig 10.1); the mustard-seed story is commentarial.

name: Bhaddā Kuṇḍalakesā
summary: Former Jain debater, ordained with the words 'Come, Bhaddā'; foremost nun in quick understanding (Thig 5.9).

name: Bhaddā Kāpilānī
summary: Wife of Mahākassapa before their renunciation; foremost nun in recollection of past lives (Thig 4.1).

name: Somā
summary: A nun who answered Māra's taunt about women's 'two-finger wisdom' (SN 5.2; Thig 3.8).

name: Vajirā
summary: A nun who answered Māra with the chariot simile: 'a being' is a convention for the heap of aggregates (SN 5.10).

name: Ubbirī
summary: A nun who mourned her daughter Jīvā until told that 84,000 Jīvās had been burned in that charnel ground (Thig 3.5).

name: Ambapālī
summary: The courtesan of Vesālī who gave the Buddha her mango grove (DN 16) and later, as a nun, reflected on her ageing body (Thig 13.1).

name: Saṅghamittā
summary: Daughter of Emperor Asoka and a bhikkhunī who, by the chronicles, brought the bhikkhunī ordination and a branch of the Bodhi tree to Laṅkā.

tradition.text: 3rd c. BCE, in the reign of Devānampiya Tissa

notes: Known from the Dīpavaṃsa and Mahāvaṃsa (not in the canon).

name: Citta the householder
summary: Householder of Macchikāsaṇḍa, a non-returner, foremost lay Dhamma teacher; his discussions with monks and with the Nigaṇṭha fill SN 41.

name: Anāthapiṇḍika
summary: The merchant Sudatta of Sāvatthī who bought Jeta's Grove for the Saṅgha; foremost lay donor; instructed on his deathbed by Sāriputta (MN 143).

name: Visākhā Migāramātā
summary: Foremost laywoman donor, builder of the Pubbārāma at Sāvatthī; the uposatha teaching of AN 3.70 was addressed to her.

name: Visākha (lay follower)
summary: The lay follower, former husband of Dhammadinnā, who questioned her in MN 44.

name: Nakulapitā
summary: An aged householder of Bhagga told to be 'afflicted in body but not in mind' (SN 22.1); with his wife Nakulamātā foremost among trusting lay followers.

name: Nakulamātā
summary: Wife of Nakulapitā, whose counsel to her sick husband is praised in AN 6.16.

name: Mahānāma the Sakyan
summary: A Sakyan lay follower, the Buddha's cousin, to whom the six recollections (AN 6.10, AN 11.11–12) were taught.

name: Jīvaka Komārabhacca
summary: Physician to King Bimbisāra and the Saṅgha; brought Ajātasattu to the Buddha (DN 2); MN 55 addressed to him.

name: Khujjuttarā
summary: Maid of Queen Sāmāvatī who, by tradition, heard and repeated the Itivuttaka; foremost laywoman in learning.

name: Dīghajāṇu
summary: Byagghapajja, a Koliyan householder taught the four sources of welfare now and hereafter (AN 8.54).

name: Sigāla
summary: A young householder worshipping the six directions, taught the lay discipline (DN 31).

name: Tapussa and Bhallika
summary: Two merchants who offered the newly awakened Buddha food and became the first lay followers, taking the two refuges (Vin Mv 1.4).
notes: Two persons in one entry, as the texts always pair them.

name: Cunda the smith
summary: The smith of Pāvā who served the Buddha his last meal (DN 16); the teaching on purity of AN 10.176 was given to a Cunda the smith of Pāvā.

name: Suddhodana
summary: The Buddha's father, a Sakyan chief of Kapilavatthu, at whose request the rule on parental consent for going forth was made (Vin Mv 1.54).

name: Māyā
summary: The Buddha's mother, who died seven days after his birth (MN 123; DN 14 as a norm of bodhisattas' mothers).

name: Rāhulamātā
summary: The bodhisatta's wife and mother of Rāhula, called 'Rāhula's mother' in the Vinaya (Mv 1.54); the name Yasodharā is commentarial.

name: Bimbisāra
summary: King of Magadha, patron of the Buddha, donor of the Bamboo Grove; at his suggestion the uposatha was instituted (Vin Mv 2.1).

name: Ajātasattu
summary: King of Magadha who killed his father Bimbisāra and later confessed to the Buddha (DN 2).

name: Pasenadi
summary: King of Kosala and lay follower, questioner in SN 3 and MN 87–90.

name: Mallikā
summary: Queen of Kosala; her dialogue with Pasenadi on whether anyone is dearer than oneself led to Ud 5.1.

name: Gaṇaka Moggallāna
summary: A brahmin accountant who asked about gradual training (MN 107).

name: Subha Todeyyaputta
summary: A young brahmin who asked why beings are inferior and superior (MN 135).

name: Assalāyana
summary: A young brahmin chosen to defend the brahmins' claims against the Buddha (MN 93).

name: Vāseṭṭha
summary: A young brahmin who, with Bhāradvāja, asked whether one is a brahmin by birth or by deeds (MN 98 / Snp 3.9) and questioned the Buddha on union with Brahmā (DN 13); in DN 27 a Vāseṭṭha is a novice.
notes: The Vāseṭṭhas of DN 13, DN 27 and MN 98 may not be the same person.

name: Bhāradvāja (the student)
summary: Vāseṭṭha's companion in MN 98 / Snp 3.9 and DN 13.

name: Kāpaṭika Bhāradvāja
summary: A sixteen-year-old brahmin student who questioned the Buddha on preserving and awakening to truth (MN 95).

name: Doṇa
summary: A brahmin who asked whether the Buddha was a god, gandhabba, yakkha or human (AN 4.36).

name: Kasibhāradvāja
summary: A brahmin farmer answered with the simile of spiritual ploughing (Snp 1.4; SN 7.11); he went forth and became an arahant.

name: Saṅgārava
summary: A brahmin taught the water similes for the hindrances (SN 46.55).

name: Māgaṇḍiya (MN 75)
summary: A wanderer of the Bhāradvāja clan who held the Buddha a 'destroyer of growth' and was taught that health is the highest gain and nibbāna the highest bliss (MN 75).
notes: Distinct from the brahmin Māgaṇḍiya of Snp 4.9.

name: Upāli the householder
summary: A wealthy lay follower of the Nigaṇṭhas who, sent to refute the Buddha, became his follower (MN 56).

name: Vacchagotta
summary: A wanderer who repeatedly questioned the Buddha on the self and the undeclared (MN 71–73; SN 44.7–11); he went forth and became an arahant (MN 73).

name: Poṭṭhapāda
summary: A wanderer who asked about the cessation of perception and the self (DN 9).

name: Jambukhādaka
summary: A wanderer, Sāriputta's nephew by commentarial account, who asked what nibbāna is (SN 38).

name: Kaccānagotta
summary: A monk who asked what right view is (SN 12.15).

name: Pukkusāti
summary: A clansman who had gone forth for the Buddha without having met him, taught the six elements in a potter's shed (MN 140); he died a non-returner.

name: Upaka
summary: An Ājīvika ascetic who met the newly awakened Buddha on the road to Benares and did not accept his claim (MN 26; Vin Mv 1.6).

name: Āḷāra Kālāma
summary: A teacher of the bodhisatta who taught the attainment of the sphere of nothingness and offered to share leadership of his community (MN 26, MN 36).

name: Uddaka Rāmaputta
summary: A teacher of the bodhisatta who taught the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception realised by his father Rāma (MN 26, MN 36).
notes: Known only through Buddhist texts; the text distinguishes Rāma, who had attained it, from Uddaka.

name: Brahmā Sahampati
summary: The Great Brahmā who implored the newly awakened Buddha to teach (SN 6.1; MN 26; Vin Mv 1.5) and spoke verses at the parinibbāna (DN 16).

name: Ajita (Pārāyana)
summary: One of the sixteen brahmin students of Bāvarī who questioned the Buddha in the Pārāyanavagga (Snp 5.2).

name: Upasīva
summary: One of the sixteen brahmin students of Bāvarī who questioned the Buddha in the Pārāyanavagga (Snp 5.7).

name: Mogharāja
summary: One of the sixteen brahmin students of Bāvarī who questioned the Buddha in the Pārāyanavagga (Snp 5.16).

name: Vipassī
summary: The first of the seven Buddhas of DN 14, ninety-one aeons ago, whose life is narrated as the model of a bodhisatta's career.

name: Sikhī
summary: The second of the seven Buddhas of DN 14 (thirty-one aeons ago).

name: Vessabhū
summary: The third of the seven Buddhas of DN 14 (thirty-one aeons ago).

name: Kakusandha
summary: The fourth of the seven Buddhas of DN 14, the first of this fortunate aeon.

name: Koṇāgamana
summary: The fifth of the seven Buddhas of DN 14.

name: Kassapa (Buddha)
summary: The sixth of the seven Buddhas of DN 14, the Buddha immediately before Gotama.

name: Dīpaṅkara
summary: The Buddha at whose feet the ascetic Sumedha vowed to become a Buddha (Buddhavaṃsa 2), the first of the twenty-four Buddhas who predicted Gotama's Buddhahood.

name: Metteyya
summary: The future Buddha who will arise when human life reaches eighty thousand years (DN 26).

name: Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta
summary: The elder who objected to the ten points of the Vajjian monks and called the Second Council at Vesālī (Cv 12).

name: Revata of Soreyya
summary: A senior elder consulted on the ten points who questioned Sabbakāmī at the Second Council (Cv 12).

name: Sabbakāmī
summary: The most senior elder (by tradition a pupil of Ānanda) who judged the ten points at the Second Council (Cv 12).

name: Moggaliputta Tissa
summary: The elder who, by the Theravāda chronicles and commentaries, presided over the Third Council at Pāṭaliputta under Asoka, purified the Saṅgha, composed the Kathāvatthu and sent missions abroad.

tradition.text: 218 years after the parinibbāna (c. 325 BCE on the tradition's count)

scholarly.text: 3rd c. BCE, if historical; the council is not mentioned in Asoka's inscriptions

notes: Account from the Dīpavaṃsa, Mahāvaṃsa and Samantapāsādikā; U37 owns the Kathāvatthu.

name: Asoka
summary: Maurya emperor whose edicts promote Dhamma and name Buddhist texts (Bairāṭ/Bhabru edict); in the Theravāda chronicles patron of the Third Council and father of Mahinda and Saṅghamittā.

name: Mahinda
summary: Son of Asoka and pupil of Moggaliputta Tissa who, by the chronicles, brought the Dhamma to Laṅkā, converting King Devānampiya Tissa at Mihintale, and founded the Mahāvihāra tradition; the commentaries were held to have been brought by him.

tradition.text: arrived in Laṅkā 236 years after the parinibbāna

name: Devānampiya Tissa
summary: King of Laṅkā converted by Mahinda; founder of the Mahāvihāra at Anurādhapura (chronicle account).

name: Vaṭṭagāmaṇī Abhaya
summary: King of Laṅkā in whose reign, by the chronicles, the Tipiṭaka and its commentary were written down at the Āloka-vihāra (Aluvihāra) for fear of their loss.

name: Nāgasena
summary: The monk who answers King Milinda in the Milindapañha (chariot simile, the flame).

name: Milinda
summary: The Indo-Greek king (Menander I) whose questions to Nāgasena form the Milindapañha.
